html:
The Acadian Peninsula (UK) on the map in 1783 and 1800 is British Nova Scotia, with Cape Breton and Prince Edward Island, on the Atlantic coast of what is now Canada.

This was once French Acadia, settled from 1604 among the Mi'kmaq. Britain took Port Royal in 1710 and gained the peninsula in the Peace of Utrecht of 1713. It founded Halifax as a naval base in 1749. Fearing the French-speaking Acadians would side with France, Britain carried out the Expulsion of the Acadians from 1755, and after 1763 it held all of the region.

When the American Revolution ended in 1783, tens of thousands of Loyalists came north, among them Black Loyalists who had won freedom by joining the British. So many came that the mainland part was split off as New Brunswick in 1784. Nova Scotia joined Canada at Confederation in 1867.
sum: The Acadian Peninsula (UK) on the map in 1783 and 1800 is British Nova Scotia, with Cape Breton and Prince Edward Island, on the Atlantic coast of what is now Canada.
